finding.claim: SQL injection (ORDER BY clause): list_users_sorted() concatenates the raw $_GET['sort'] value into the query. Prepared statements are not used, and there is no allowlist. An unauthenticated attacker can inject SQL, for example a CASE/subquery boolean-blind payload in ORDER BY, to read arbitrary data from the SQLite database.
finding.sink: $pdo->query("SELECT id, name FROM users ORDER BY " . $sort) (list.php:6)

trace.note: $sort = $_GET['sort'] ?? 'id' takes the user-controlled value with no validation
$sort is concatenated into the SQL string and run through PDO::query()

finding.guards_checked: There is no allowlist, cast or escaping on the path. The sibling function list_users_safe() (list.php:10-11) maps the value through an allowlist, and find_user() (list.php:16-17) uses a bound parameter. list_users_sorted() has neither, so it is the unprotected one. The repo contains no callers of list_users_sorted(), and the file has no auth check. The finding assumes another script includes list.php and calls the function.

verdict.reason: list.php:5-6 does concatenate raw $_GET['sort'] into PDO::query() with no allowlist (unlike list_users_safe at list.php:10-12), but list_users_sorted() is never called anywhere in the repo and list.php only defines functions, so whether an attacker can reach it depends on code outside the repo.
